newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power steady amid tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power steady amid tight supplies.

text.p: Spot power in the western U.S. held steady Friday after firming during the week amid news of scattered, unplanned power plant outages.
California-Oregon border electricity for Monday was quoted $17.50-18.00, unchanged from next-day schedulings on Thursday. Saturday COB was assessed at $17.00, while Sunday was at $16.50.
Mid-Columbia was holding at $18.00-19.00, while Midway was quoted $19.00-20.00 for Monday.
Palo Verde was last at $20.00-21.00, unchanged from Thursday.
Traders cited the delayed restart of coal-fired units at PacifiCorp's Jim Bridger, Wyo. and Centralia Wash. plants as helping to tighten the market.

In addition, unplanned outages of a 790 MW unit at Southern California Edison Co's Mohave coal-fired plant, on Wednesday, and the company's 1,080 MW San Onofre nuclear unit 2, on Tuesday, cut into regional power supplies.
"All the lines are full going south," said a California trader. "At the same time, the water situation is thinning out."
October COB was last quoted $16.50-17.00, up from $16.25-16.50 on Thursday. Palo Verde for October was quoted $17.00-17.20, up from $16.25-16.50 on Thursday.
